goal: First add a lastLoginAt field to the backend user data structure, then make the frontend profile page display the value of that field.

tasks.title: Add lastLoginAt field to backend user data structure
tasks.description: In this repository, locate the backend's user data structure (search for a User type/interface/class/schema under apps/server/src and packages/*/src, e.g. anywhere defining fields like id, email, or name for an end-user/account record; if no such user model exists yet, create a minimal one at apps/server/src/models/user.ts with at least id and email fields, and export it). Add a new field `lastLoginAt` typed as an ISO-8601 string (or `Date | null` if the codebase already uses Date objects elsewhere for timestamps — match existing convention, e.g. check how `createdAt`/`updatedAt` are typed on Agent in packages/core/src/agent/types.ts and mirror that style). Make the field optional/nullable (`lastLoginAt?: string | null`) since not all existing user records will have a value. If there's a REST endpoint that returns user data (e.g. under apps/server/src/index.ts or apps/server/src/routes), ensure `lastLoginAt` is included in the serialized response. If a login/auth handler exists, update it to set `lastLoginAt` to the current timestamp on successful login; otherwise just add the field to the data structure and its type definition without wiring up write logic. Run any existing type-check/build command (e.g. `npm run build` or `tsc --noEmit`) in the affected package to confirm no type errors were introduced.

tasks.title: Display lastLoginAt on frontend profile page
tasks.description: In this repository's frontend (apps/web/src), locate the page/component that displays a user's profile information (search for a ProfilePage component, or if none exists, the relevant section of apps/web/src/App.tsx that renders user/account details). If no dedicated profile page exists, add a simple profile section/component that fetches the current user object from the backend (matching however other data is fetched in apps/web/src/ws/client.ts or via existing fetch calls in App.tsx) and renders it. Add a `lastLoginAt` field to the frontend's local TypeScript type for the user object so it matches the field name and type added on the backend (check apps/server for the exact field name/type first — it must be `lastLoginAt` as a string ISO timestamp or null). Render the value as a human-readable formatted date/time (e.g. using `toLocaleString()` or a small date-formatting helper), with a sensible fallback label like 'Never logged in' when the value is null/undefined. Verify the frontend builds/type-checks successfully (e.g. `npm run build` or `tsc --noEmit` in apps/web).
